title.value: AfriQA: Cross-lingual Open-Retrieval Question Answering for African Languages
title.justification: The title is explicitly mentioned at the beginning of the paper and covers the topic of cross-lingual open-retrieval question answering focused on African languages.
title.quote: AfriQA: Cross-lingual Open-Retrieval Question Answering for African Languages Odunayo Ogundepo1,∗,∗, Tajuddeen R. Gwadabe∗,∗, Clara E. Rivera2 , Jonathan H. Clark2 , Sebastian Ruder2 , David Ifeoluwa Adelani3,∗ , etc.

extractions.description: The paper presents AfriQA, the first cross-lingual open-retrieval question answering dataset focused on African languages. It seeks to improve information accessibility for speakers of under-represented African languages by providing a dataset that facilitates QA technology development for these languages. The paper includes 12,000+ examples across 10 African languages and evaluates baseline QA systems' performance, highlighting challenges in current translation and retrieval methods.

climate_change_is_central.justification: Although the paper addresses inclusivity and accessibility in technology for under-represented languages, it does not relate directly to climate change. Its primary focus is on language diversity and technology development.
climate_change_is_central.quote: In this work, we take a step toward bridging the information gap between native speakers of many African languages and the vast amount of digital information available on the web by creating AfriQA, the first open-retrieval cross-lingual QA dataset focused on African languages.
